highlights: # Kimi-maker Moonshot AI targets $2 billion in annual revenue. One of China’s most prominent AI labs, Moonshot AI, believes it can turn its popular open-weight model into serious sales growth. On Friday, Bloomberg reported that the lab is targeting $2 billion in annualized revenue by the end of the year, double the company’s reported revenue run rate for August. It’s an aggressive goal that reflects the success of the company’s K3 model since its release this summer. Moonshot’s projected revenue is still dwarfed by that of OpenAI and Anthropic, which recent reports put at $40 billion and $65 billion respectively. The rising projections show there’s still money to be made from open-weight AI models, even if they’re not as lucrative as closed-weight frontier models. Earlier this week, Anthropic accused the company of a long-running model distillation campaign that routed nearly 300,000 requests from Kimi directly to Claude Opus, effectively serving Opus in place of Kimi’s own models.

Now a new bot called Instinct is outperforming the AI giants. Instinct lets people ask for help with all kinds of tasks by texting the bot directly through iMessage or WhatsApp. Lately, it has been all the rage in the tech world. When AI agents have access to your email inbox and credit-card information, all sorts of strange things can go wrong. (Compare that with ChatGPT, which is always vomiting up walls of text and asking goading follow-up questions.) When I gave my agent a $25 budget and asked it to surprise my editor with a book, the bot read his previous writing (at my instruction), found a book he might enjoy—*Material World* by Ed Conway—and sent an email alerting him that it was ready for pick-up at his local Barnes & Noble.

highlights: Agentic AI is creating a ‘paradigm shift’ in semiconductor design, chairman of domestic EDA leader Empyrean Technology says. Artificial intelligence agents are increasingly taking the wheel in designing China’s next-generation semiconductors, as Beijing and domestic technology firms accelerate efforts to integrate AI into chip design software to bolster national self-sufficiency. Empyrean Technology, China’s top maker of electronic design automation (EDA) tools, has been accelerating the chip design process by using AI-optimised algorithms and agentic tools, according to company chairman Liu Weiping. Agentic AI has brought a “paradigm shift” to chip design, moving away from “humans operating tools” to “humans commanding agents”, Liu said at the 2026 International Integrated Circuit Innovation Expo in Shenzhen on Wednesday. Empyrean was developing an agentic EDA platform, which the company considered core to its future strategy, that would allow its own agentic tools to work with its partners’ agents, according to Liu.

latest.title: Panmnesia and Meta Propose CXL-Based AI Datacenter Architecture in Nature Journal - Wowtale
latest.summary: # Panmnesia and Meta Propose CXL-Based AI Datacenter Architecture in Nature Journal. AI infrastructure startup Panmnesia and global hyperscaler Meta have jointly proposed a next-generation AI datacent...
highlights: # Panmnesia and Meta Propose CXL-Based AI Datacenter Architecture in Nature Journal. AI infrastructure startup Panmnesia and global hyperscaler Meta have jointly proposed a next-generation AI datacenter architecture that operates an entire datacenter as a single chip. The study centers on integrating CPUs, accelerators, and memory into a single datacenter-scale domain based on the CXL (Compute Express Link) standard. To address this, the Panmnesia and Meta research team extended chip-internal design principles to datacenter scale. Inside a chip, CPU cores, accelerators, and memory connect through short, uniform pathways that carry signals in constant time; they share a single memory space and hardware automatically enforces data coherence. “This research is significant in proposing the direction for next-generation AI infrastructure, where an entire datacenter operates as a single computing system based on CXL.”. To extend the scale-up domain across an entire datacenter, the research team proposes a next step: keeping the rest of the design unchanged and switching from electrical to optical signals (CXL-over-Optics).

highlights: # The US and China are racing to build ‘self-improving AI’. Both sides view ‘recursive self-improvement’ as a game-changer in the AI race. The US-China race for artificial intelligence dominance has entered a new phase: using AI to build better AI. The ultimate goal is to achieve what the industry refers to as recursive self-improvement (RSI) – the creation of AI systems that can train themselves autonomously. RSI has the potential to be a game-changer for the AI industry. As AI systems contribute to building more capable successors, which in turn become better at improving the next generation, the process could create an accelerating feedback loop – propelling the evolution of AI onto a new trajectory. In a blog post last week**,** OpenAI said it aimed to build an automated AI researcher capable of advancing deep learning research, though it was still unsure “how to safely get all the way to aligned, full RSI”.

today.title: It’s All Fun and Games Until You Give AI Your Credit Card - The Atlantic
today.summary: # It’s All Fun and Games Until You Give AI Your Credit Card. AI personal assistants are now acting on people’s behalf in the real world—and all sorts of strange things are going wrong. Now a new bot c...
highlights: # It’s All Fun and Games Until You Give AI Your Credit Card. AI personal assistants are now acting on people’s behalf in the real world—and all sorts of strange things are going wrong. Now a new bot called Instinct is outperforming the AI giants. Instinct lets people ask for help with all kinds of tasks by texting the bot directly through iMessage or WhatsApp. Lately, it has been all the rage in the tech world. When AI agents have access to your email inbox and credit-card information, all sorts of strange things can go wrong. (Compare that with ChatGPT, which is always vomiting up walls of text and asking goading follow-up questions.) When I gave my agent a $25 budget and asked it to surprise my editor with a book, the bot read his previous writing (at my instruction), found a book he might enjoy—*Material World* by Ed Conway—and sent an email alerting him that it was ready for pick-up at his local Barnes & Noble.

highlights: Agentic AI is creating a ‘paradigm shift’ in semiconductor design, chairman of domestic EDA leader Empyrean Technology says. Artificial intelligence agents are increasingly taking the wheel in designing China’s next-generation semiconductors, as Beijing and domestic technology firms accelerate efforts to integrate AI into chip design software to bolster national self-sufficiency. Empyrean Technology, China’s top maker of electronic design automation (EDA) tools, has been accelerating the chip design process by using AI-optimised algorithms and agentic tools, according to company chairman Liu Weiping. Agentic AI has brought a “paradigm shift” to chip design, moving away from “humans operating tools” to “humans commanding agents”, Liu said at the 2026 International Integrated Circuit Innovation Expo in Shenzhen on Wednesday. Empyrean was developing an agentic EDA platform, which the company considered core to its future strategy, that would allow its own agentic tools to work with its partners’ agents, according to Liu.

today.title: Panmnesia and Meta Propose CXL-Based AI Datacenter Architecture in Nature Journal - Wowtale
today.summary: # Panmnesia and Meta Propose CXL-Based AI Datacenter Architecture in Nature Journal. AI infrastructure startup Panmnesia and global hyperscaler Meta have jointly proposed a next-generation AI datacent...
highlights: # Panmnesia and Meta Propose CXL-Based AI Datacenter Architecture in Nature Journal. AI infrastructure startup Panmnesia and global hyperscaler Meta have jointly proposed a next-generation AI datacenter architecture that operates an entire datacenter as a single chip. The study centers on integrating CPUs, accelerators, and memory into a single datacenter-scale domain based on the CXL (Compute Express Link) standard. To address this, the Panmnesia and Meta research team extended chip-internal design principles to datacenter scale. Inside a chip, CPU cores, accelerators, and memory connect through short, uniform pathways that carry signals in constant time; they share a single memory space and hardware automatically enforces data coherence. “This research is significant in proposing the direction for next-generation AI infrastructure, where an entire datacenter operates as a single computing system based on CXL.”. To extend the scale-up domain across an entire datacenter, the research team proposes a next step: keeping the rest of the design unchanged and switching from electrical to optical signals (CXL-over-Optics).

today.summary: # The US and China are racing to build ‘self-improving AI’. Both sides view ‘recursive self-improvement’ as a game-changer in the AI race. The US-China race for artificial intelligence dominance has e...
highlights: # The US and China are racing to build ‘self-improving AI’. Both sides view ‘recursive self-improvement’ as a game-changer in the AI race. The US-China race for artificial intelligence dominance has entered a new phase: using AI to build better AI. The ultimate goal is to achieve what the industry refers to as recursive self-improvement (RSI) – the creation of AI systems that can train themselves autonomously. RSI has the potential to be a game-changer for the AI industry. As AI systems contribute to building more capable successors, which in turn become better at improving the next generation, the process could create an accelerating feedback loop – propelling the evolution of AI onto a new trajectory. In a blog post last week**,** OpenAI said it aimed to build an automated AI researcher capable of advancing deep learning research, though it was still unsure “how to safely get all the way to aligned, full RSI”.

week.summary: # Kimi-maker Moonshot AI targets $2 billion in annual revenue. One of China’s most prominent AI labs, Moonshot AI, believes it can turn its popular open-weight model into serious sales growth. On Frid...
highlights: # Kimi-maker Moonshot AI targets $2 billion in annual revenue. One of China’s most prominent AI labs, Moonshot AI, believes it can turn its popular open-weight model into serious sales growth. On Friday, Bloomberg reported that the lab is targeting $2 billion in annualized revenue by the end of the year, double the company’s reported revenue run rate for August. It’s an aggressive goal that reflects the success of the company’s K3 model since its release this summer. Moonshot’s projected revenue is still dwarfed by that of OpenAI and Anthropic, which recent reports put at $40 billion and $65 billion respectively. The rising projections show there’s still money to be made from open-weight AI models, even if they’re not as lucrative as closed-weight frontier models. Earlier this week, Anthropic accused the company of a long-running model distillation campaign that routed nearly 300,000 requests from Kimi directly to Claude Opus, effectively serving Opus in place of Kimi’s own models.

month.title: Kimi-maker Moonshot AI targets $2 billion in annual revenue - TechCrunch
month.summary: # Kimi-maker Moonshot AI targets $2 billion in annual revenue. One of China’s most prominent AI labs, Moonshot AI, believes it can turn its popular open-weight model into serious sales growth. On Frid...
highlights: # Kimi-maker Moonshot AI targets $2 billion in annual revenue. One of China’s most prominent AI labs, Moonshot AI, believes it can turn its popular open-weight model into serious sales growth. On Friday, Bloomberg reported that the lab is targeting $2 billion in annualized revenue by the end of the year, double the company’s reported revenue run rate for August. It’s an aggressive goal that reflects the success of the company’s K3 model since its release this summer. Moonshot’s projected revenue is still dwarfed by that of OpenAI and Anthropic, which recent reports put at $40 billion and $65 billion respectively. The rising projections show there’s still money to be made from open-weight AI models, even if they’re not as lucrative as closed-weight frontier models. Earlier this week, Anthropic accused the company of a long-running model distillation campaign that routed nearly 300,000 requests from Kimi directly to Claude Opus, effectively serving Opus in place of Kimi’s own models.
